data.title: Checkbox
data.tagline: Choose one, several, or none of the options
data.description: Checkboxes work for interests, filters, and other choices that are independent of one another. A single checkbox can also confirm one statement. If exactly one option must be selected, use Radio instead.

avoid: Use checkboxes for choices that exclude each other
Preselect consent that the user should give knowingly
Make the clickable label too small
Leave the effect of selecting a parent item unclear

lessonPractice.title: A subscription form offers email, SMS, and app notifications. People may choose several or none, and changes apply on submit. What fits?

options.label: Give each notification channel its own checkbox
options.feedback: The channels are independent, and checkboxes express choosing one, several, or none accurately.

options.label: Put all three channels in one radio group
options.feedback: A radio group keeps only one choice, incorrectly preventing people from selecting several channels.

options.label: Use three immediate switches and still keep a Submit button
options.feedback: Switches normally signal immediate change, which conflicts with the form's apply-on-submit behavior.

data.agentPrompt: Use three independent checkboxes for email, SMS, and app notifications, allowing several or none, and apply them on submit. Verify clickable labels and the submitted channel values.
